[2026-08-17 | AMZN | Underweight | +0.3% | +1.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN at 261.31 is Underweight: reduce, do not exit, do not add. Trim roughly 35–40% of existing exposure in two tranches — half at or near the current reference or into any 263–265 bounce, half as a limit bid in the 265.19–265.50 supply cluster (10 EMA 265.19 / rising VWMA 265.27 / 38.2% retrace 265.49); if that limit does not fill and AMZN closes below 257.09, complete the remaining trim at market rather than waiting for a better bid the structure says will not come. Carry the residual at ~60–65% of a standard allocation, sized so a gap to the 248.32 (50 SMA) structural line costs no more than ~0.4–0.5% of equity, and assume slippage beyond any stop with ATR at 8.12 (3.1% of price). Escalate to 25–30% of standard weight on a close below 257.09 on >50M shares or two consecutive closes below it; a close below 248.32 takes the residual to tracking size. Rebuild only on two consecutive closes above 265.75 on volume above the 47.8M 21-session average with the MACD histogram turning positive — and then only to 80–90% of standard with the risk point reset at 257.6.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is settled; the debate is about degree and execution. Three verifiable items decide it.

1) THE PAYOFF MAP IS NEGATIVE AND NOBODY CONTESTED IT. From 261.31 with the structural line at the 50 SMA (248.32), risk is 12.99 points (4.97%). The first two targets — 274.48 and 278.09 — pay only 1.01:1 and 1.29:1, and even the top of the range at 287.20 pays 1.99:1. Downside to the 237.9–239.8 gap-fill / 200-SMA confluence is ~9%. The aggressive analyst's advertised 3:1 required the bottom of the buy zone and the top of the target range simultaneously. The tape corroborates it one-sidedly: close below the 10 EMA (265.19), below the rising VWMA (265.27), rejection of the 265.75 session high, first negative MACD histogram (−0.310) since 2026-07-30, lowest close of the entire post-gap period, back inside the pre-gap range ceiling (~278.56), on 43.90M shares (1.33x the five-session average) on a down day, with RSI 52.43 leaving no oversold cushion. This is the same configuration that made the 2026-08-10 Underweight pay (−6.0% raw and alpha in five days), and that reflection's lesson is load-bearing: lead with the reward-to-risk arithmetic and pre-committed structural exits, and do not let stacked moving averages soften the trim.

2) EARNINGS QUALITY IS IMPAIRED AND THE BULL'S DEFENSE CONFLATED TWO THINGS. The $122.3B private-stake line (up from $16.2B in six months, ~21% of implied book equity, driving ~62% of Q2 EPS) is a Level-3 mark, not the aggressive analyst's \"hard, monetizable IPO catalyst\"; a 20% haircut is ~$24B pre-tax, larger than an entire quarter of operating income. His \"assume it is worth zero\" framing answered a write-down nobody proposed, while ignoring that a flat quarter against a $5.75 consensus print reads as an earnings collapse. The +$41.44B TTM deferred tax expense swing (vs −$2.41B prior) arrives at the same time cash taxes normalize from a 4.9% effective rate (each 10pp step toward 22–24% costs roughly $25–30B of FCF) — they do not offset in time. Balance-sheet direction is adverse: LT debt $68.84B → $133.00B (+93.2%), interest expense +155%, net interest negative for the first time, TTM FCF −$11.63B versus +$13.48B a year ago, 1.03x current ratio, ~$94.7B of fixed twelve-month obligations, and $54B/quarter of capex at 25.8% of revenue meaning the depreciation bill has not landed. The $650B of contractual obligations is a commitment to pay, not customer backlog.

3) THE RE-ACCELERATION CANNOT BE VERIFIED AS ORGANIC. H1 2026 acquisitions were $39.77B, with $24.36B in Q2 alone, against a Q2 revenue increase of $32.9B, and the supplied set has no segment revenue and no 10-Q business-combination footnote. The supporting material itself warns against extrapolating the ~20% rate without that footnote. AR +30.1% versus revenue +18.2% with allowance coverage down from 3.54% to 3.18% points the same direction. I treat organic growth as unverified, not disproven — and the conservative is right that a conservative book does not pay full weight for a number it cannot decompose.

WHERE EACH SEAT WINS ON EXECUTION. The aggressive analyst is right that the alternative to trimming is not caution but holding full exposure through a bracket whose 2026-08-17 range alone was 7.41 points with a 9% downside branch — but his execution is too optimistic, since hanging the entire trim on a 265.19 bid sits inside the supply band the tape just rejected, and the 2026-08-07 GOOGL reflection records precisely that error (a resting limit filled on momentum, not on stabilization). The conservative's split-order point wins and I adopt it. Where he overreaches: (a) treating missing evidence as confirmed bearish when net debt/EBITDA ~0.4x, $176.1B of cash and securities, Q2 OCF $45.39B (+39.6%), operating margin 13.69% (+226bp) with marketing +3.9% and G&A −3.9% against revenue +18.2%, and rising 50/200 SMAs establish no solvency and no permanent-capital-loss case — hence trim, not exit, and not a short; (b) his blanket ≤40%-of-standard residual cap and refusal to rebuild beyond half weight until 278.09–278.56, which repeats the pattern that cost 15–20% alpha across five prior AMZN Underweights struck inside an intact rising 200-SMA structure; and (c) halving the residual on a first support break regardless of volume. The neutral analyst's calibration is the seat I adopt — two-tranche execution for certainty, no hostage-taking on a bounce the structure says may not come, residual sized to a survivable gap, and a two-close rebuild filter rather than the trader's single-close trigger, because ATR of 8.12 makes one 1.7% close pure noise and would whipsaw the caller back into the same supply band. Where I side against the neutral: the rebuild, once earned, goes to 80–90% of standard, not a token add, because the operating evidence entitles the franchise to that much.

WHY UNDERWEIGHT AND NOT SELL. Operating performance is not deteriorating: Q2 OCF +39.6%, core EPS ~+28.6% after stripping marks, 0.4x net debt/EBITDA, $176.1B liquidity, price +5.2% above a rising 50 SMA and +9.9% above a rising 200 SMA with MACD still above zero. There is no solvency case and no permanent-capital-loss case. The trader's \"Sell\" label describes a partial reduction, which on this scale is Underweight; a full exit would forfeit the franchise and the residual optionality at the exact moment the arithmetic supports only shrinking.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE CALL. Upgrades: two consecutive closes above 265.75 on >47.8M with a positive MACD histogram (partial rebuild to 80–90% of standard); a close above 278.09–278.56 (full standard weight); or fundamental confirmation — the 10-Q business-combination footnote showing organic growth of ~18–20%, capex growth decelerating below OCF growth while cash taxes remain contained (both together, not one), purchase obligations flattening, or trailing FCF turning positive. Downgrades to Sell: a close below 257.09 opening 254.03 → 248.32 → 237.9–239.8; a close below 248.32 invalidating the constructive trend; or any impairment or flat-mark quarter on the $122.3B private stake, which is a downgrade trigger rather than a neutral event given it is ~21% of book equity and drives most of reported EPS.

DATA GAPS NOT UNDERWRITTEN TO EITHER SIDE: no AWS segment revenue or operating income, no organic-versus-inorganic revenue split, no 10-Q business-combination footnote, no disclosed mark-to-model assumptions behind the $122.3B asset, no Q3 guidance or consensus, and 194 of 214 news records absent from the supplied set. The July retail sales −0.6% print (non-store retail exposed) is a second-hand weekend headline and should not carry the bear case, but neither should the Anthropic–AWS \"$11.5B Q2 revenue\" read-through or the stale June 30 13F cluster (Coatue/Viking adds against Soros/Third Point cuts) carry the bull case — all three are low-signal. No portfolio, holdings, or cash context was supplied, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation.

**Price Target**: 252.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
The five-day window shows +0.3% raw and +1.5% alpha versus SPY, meaning AMZN modestly outperformed the benchmark — the opposite of what an Underweight wants — but at 0.1x the 8.12 ATR this is pure noise and far too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis. What it does undercut is the tape-based timing layer: the close below the 10 EMA/VWMA, first negative MACD histogram, and lowest close of the post-gap period produced no downside follow-through, and neither the 257.09 escalation nor the 248.32 invalidation was ever tested. What it supports is the trim-not-exit construction: the residual 60–65% weight cost nothing, and the franchise strength cited against the conservative seat (0.4x net debt/EBITDA, +39.6% OCF, rising 50/200 SMAs) held up. Lesson for the next AMZN call: price the Underweight off the payoff map and the unverifiable Level-3 mark/FCF items, which are multi-quarter, and stop letting a single-session negative tape configuration carry the timing argument — state the ±1 ATR noise band up front so a five-day drift cannot be mistaken for confirmation.

[2026-08-14 | AMZN | Underweight | -1.5% | -0.2% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN at $262.65 — reduce, do not exit, and do not short. Trim ~40–50% of any existing AMZN position down to ~50–60% of a standard single-name allocation, using hybrid execution rather than parking the whole trim above the market: sell a meaningful first slice at/near the market (262.65) or on a limit at the VWMA of 263.41 so the risk reduction actually happens, a second slice at 263.41, and an opportunistic final slice at the 10 EMA of 266.05. Manage the retained stub in two tiers — a decisive close below 248.17 or an intraday break of 246.30 reduces the stub further, while 237.70 (rising 200 SMA) remains the true structural invalidation for a small residual core. Rebuild only in staged size: 10–15% of standard weight at 250.25–256.52 only on a *closing* stabilization (not a touch), another 10–15% at 248.17 only if that shelf holds, a tactical re-add to standard weight on a close above 266.05 on ≥35M shares, and the final third — plus any move above standard weight — only on proof (capex guidance below ~$110B, D&A decelerating as a % of revenue, or AWS growth above ~30%). Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: **All three seats agree on reduction; the disagreement is mechanical, and the mechanics resolve in favor of a real trim, not a smart one.** The aggressive, conservative and neutral analysts converge on the destination — AMZN at $262.65 does not deserve full standard weight — and disagree only on how to get there and how to get back in. That makes this a sizing decision, and on sizing the conservative and neutral seats beat the aggressive. The aggressive's "risk arbitrage" framing is wrong and both other seats correctly dismantled it: nothing here is hedged, the 263.41/266.05 limits sit 29bp and 130bp *above* a 262.65 close rather than being "a live bid," and the very MACD evidence the aggressive cites (histogram +3.904 → +0.392 in four sessions, third close below the 10 EMA at 266.05, first meaningful close below VWMA 263.41) argues a bounce to 266.05 is the less likely near-term sequence. "Either resolution pays us" also ignores the third path the neutral named: AMZN drifts between ~256 and 266, neither the 248–257 ladder nor the 266.05 reclaim fires, and the book is left underweight with friction and no mechanism back in. That third path is the one the prior 2026-08-07 AMZN decision warned about in reverse — and it is why I front-load part of the trim near the market instead of pre-committing the whole reduction to a bounce that may not arrive.

**Why reduce at all: the fundamental case is one-sided against full weight, and the prior call's own lesson says let size carry it.** The research plan's evidence is specific and largely unrebutted. The margin-bridge decomposition is the decisive item: of the +226bp of operating margin expansion booked *through* an 88bp D&A headwind, roughly 225bp came from opex self-help — marketing down 98bp as a share of revenue, SBC down 89bp, G&A down 38bp — while capex was a drag via depreciation, not the engine of the expansion. The aggressive's strongest claim ("capex is converting") is therefore an assertion about 2027–2028 that the filing does not support, and a capex-to-D&A ratio of ~2.7x in Q2 means the depreciation bill for the current buildout has not yet hit the P&L. That matters because the expansion being leaned on is finite and the offset is still ahead. Layered on top: TTM FCF of −$11.6B with H1 free cash flow after acquisitions of −$66.8B; a capital program now exceeding operating cash generation; net cash of $29.7B shrinking by $21.8B in six months and turning to roughly −$66.7B of net debt once $96.3B of operating leases are included as the research includes them; $82B of new debt issuance; interest expense +155% y/y; a 3.3% cash tax rate flattered by $30.5B of deferred tax (the single biggest threat to the "+44.2% OCF" headline); $62.8B of non-cash mark-up equal to 52% of H1 pretax income sitting on a $122.3B illiquid private-equity book marked by management; and $650B of contractual obligations, 59% of total assets. Against that, a derived ~31–32x core multiple (~$4.05 H1 core EPS, ~$8.10–8.60 annualized, on a $262.65 close) has no cushion. The aggressive cannot have it both ways — arguing the reported EPS is accounting fiction while implying the stock is cheap on that same fiction. The 2026-08-07 review is directly on point: it concluded that when the fundamental evidence is this one-sided, the *trim size*, not the distance to a structural stop, should carry the conviction. I am applying that here rather than re-litigating it.

**Why Underweight and not Sell: the trend structure and the operating engine forbid liquidation.** Revenue accelerated to +19.6% from +16.6% on a ~$200.6B quarterly base; OCF +44.2% in H1; SBC down in absolute dollars with a flat diluted share count; $176.1B of cash and AFS securities with ~21x interest coverage — solvency was never contested. Price is 10.5% above a *rising* 200 SMA at 237.70 with the golden-cross spread widening to +10.46 and VWMA climbing 240.82 → 263.41. The bear's own falsification list — hold 19%+ growth, FCF turning positive, capex guidance below ~$110B — is entirely plausible, and its ask of "$248–257 before I'd argue the long side" is a timing and valuation objection, not a broken-business thesis. Exiting here would repeat the documented pattern in this name where bearish tape reads inside a rising long-term trend carried no directional information, and would forfeit the option value of a business accelerating at $200B scale.

**Why not Hold, and why the aggressive's full ladder does not survive.** Holding full weight at $262.65 is the worst-priced choice on the board: ~1.3% to the VWMA/10 EMA cluster versus 5.4–5.6% of air to the 50 SMA at 248.17 with no support in between, and the 07-31 gap-day low at 262.01 already tested (08-14 low 262.42). That is a quarter of upside for a dollar of downside. But the aggressive's price-first ladder fails the conservative's consistency test, which the neutral correctly seconded: the same 248.17 line was dismissed as a mechanical artifact of the +15.3% gap day when it suited the bear case and elevated to a "triple-confluence shelf" when it suited the buyback case, and the plan simultaneously wanted to *buy* 248–257 while tolerating a drawdown of the *retained* stub to 237.70 — roughly 9.5% of avoidable loss on a position already judged impaired. The resolution is the neutral's two-tier structure, which I adopt: reduce the stub further on a decisive close below 248.17 or an intraday break of 246.30, and keep only a small residual core down to the 237.70 structural invalidation — so the 248–257 ladder is a *separately sized* position requiring a closing stabilization signal (a higher low or a close back above 256.52), not an add into a fired stop. With ATR at 8.17 (>3% of price), a close below 248.17 can be a volatility overshoot into 246–250 rather than clean trend failure, which is why I do not adopt the conservative's hair-trigger full exit there, and why I do not adopt the aggressive's proof-never price-only ladder either: the neutral's split — price + volume confirmation earns small size, fundamental proof earns the final third and anything above standard weight — is the correct calibration. The cross-ticker lesson from the 2026-08-06 GOOGL Underweight applies and I am building it in: put a re-risk trigger at a named level with volume confirmation (close above 266.05 on ≥35M shares → tactical re-add to standard weight) so a correct Underweight does not ossify into a permanent underweight.

**What would change the call.** Upgrade toward Hold/market weight on: a daily close above 266.05 on ≥35M shares (tape repair), or 287.20 on >50M shares (invalidation of the cap); or disclosure of capex guidance below ~$110B for H2, D&A decelerating as a percentage of revenue, AWS segment growth above ~30%, TTM FCF turning positive, long-term debt flat or declining, or any transaction validating the $122.3B private-equity marks. Downgrade toward a minimal position on: a high-volume (≥50M shares) close below 262.01 (active confirmation of the bear tape case), a decisive close below 248.17, a further +155%-style compounding in interest expense with cash continuing to fall, normalization of the 3.3% cash tax rate (the ~$14B OCF haircut), any mark-down of the $122.3B book (a 20% haircut is ~$2.25/share, roughly a full quarter of core EPS as a charge), tightening credit conditions for hyperscaler issuance, or spread of the NYC Delivery Protection Act to other cities — a cost overhang in exactly the last-mile segment generating the opex leverage the bull relies on. Full exit only on a close below the 200 SMA at 237.70, which would invalidate the long-term trend entirely.

**Data gaps stated, not papered over.** No valuation multiples were available from the tools — the ~31–32x core P/E is derived from management's stated core-EPS figures, not a reported multiple, and must be re-verified against a live quote before sizing. AWS segment revenue is absent from the extract, so the entire "AWS re-acceleration justifies capex" leg is inference plus a secondhand third-party opinion and should be treated as unconfirmed. News coverage is missing for Aug 7–12. No portfolio or holdings context was supplied, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation.

**Price Target**: 250.0
